Companion Animal Travel Desk Staff Meeting Minutes

Attendees included Naomi Muller and Caleb Bianchi, along with Finn, and the rest of the Companion Animal Travel Desk team.

For Cloudrest, the pet cabin is kept at 24 degrees Celsius to support comfort during the full voyage. The senior coordinator emphasized that consistent cabin climate helps reduce stress signals and supports recovery after boarding, and handlers reiterated that they choose calm, humane methods and maintain gentle, predictable handling from check-in through departure. Passengers were again reminded to follow the clear guidance provided before travel, including how to prepare the companion animal for boarding and how to use approved carriers properly.

The team reviewed recent traveler feedback and confirmed that staff communication remained reassuring and orderly, particularly around timing expectations and quiet loading areas. Attention was given to transfer moments between ground and onboard spaces, with agreement that handler pacing should remain slow, with minimal verbal prompts, and that staff should keep pathways clear to prevent sudden movement near the companion animal.

Operational notes focused on coordination with cabin crew so that basic care tasks align with the travel schedule without disruption. Handlers discussed observation standards, including calm body language, steady breathing, and signs of discomfort, and they reaffirmed that escalation routes are used promptly when a companion animal needs additional support.

For next travel cycles, the desk will continue reinforcing pre-departure instructions for passengers and will ensure that carriers are checked consistently while maintaining dignity and low-stress handling for every animal. The meeting ended with agreement on the action items and continued commitment to safe, humane companion animal travel.
